newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Caltex Phils says 1996 net about 20 pct under 1995.
newsitem.headline: Caltex Phils says 1996 net about 20 pct under 1995.

text.p: Caltex (Philippines) Inc's net income in 1996 was about 20 percent lower than the one billion peso profits the oil refiner posted in 1995, a company official said.

"Our earnings last year were about 20 percent off the previous year. We made one billion pesos in 1995," Masarrat Husain, Caltex director and vice-president for corporate services told reporters late on Wednesday.
The unlisted company does not release its results publically.
Husain said the country's oil industry incurred $80 million in losses last year as a result of an automatic oil pricing formula adopted prior to the full deregulation of the oil industry.

Oil refiners last year complained that the formula which made use of Singapore Posted Prices as a benchmark in adjusting domestic pump prices failed to immediately pass on the fluctuations in crude prices.
"We are expecting a recovery this year. We will be more aggressive," said Husain.

The Caltex official said the company will invest $100 million this year largely for its retail business. The $100 million is part of the $500 million Caltex earlier said it would spend in the next four years to enhance its marketing and refinery facilities in the Philippines.
Caltex (Philippines) is a unit of Caltex Petroleum Corp which is a joint venture of Chevron Corp and Texaco Inc.
